properties.title: CaO Abundance · Clementine 1D-CNN (Qiu et al., 2025)
properties.authors: Denggao Qiu, Jianguo Yan, Bin Liu
properties.processing:lineage: Clementine UVVIS DIM Mosaic (5 bands: 415, 750, 900, 950, 1000 nm, 100 m/pixel) combined with OMAT as a 6-element input vector. 1D CNN: two Conv1D layers (32 filters, kernel=2, ReLU), MaxPooling1D (pool=2), Dense(64, ReLU), single linear output. L2 regularization (0.001). Adam optimizer (lr=0.01), max 400 epochs, early stopping (patience=30), z-score normalization. Trained on 49 ground-truth points from Apollo, Luna, and Chang'E missions including Chang'E-6. CaO cannot be estimated from classical equation models. R²=0.96+ on training set; LOOCV R²=0.918.
properties.lri:data_use_note: CaO is a key component of both anorthosite (plagioclase, CaAl₂Si₂O₈) and pyroxene. High CaO in the highlands indicates calcium-rich plagioclase; in mare basalts it reflects clinopyroxene content. Complementary to Al₂O₃ for distinguishing anorthositic vs. pyroxene-dominated terrains. Calcium is a potential construction material resource (cement analog). LOOCV R²=0.918, the second-highest of the five oxides.
properties.lri:quality_note_short: 1D CNN inversion from Clementine UVVIS, calibrated with Chang'E-6 samples. LOOCV R²=0.918. Global mean 14.93 wt%. Bimodal: highland mode 16.38 wt%, mare mode 10.63 wt%. Not derivable from classical equation models.
properties.lri:quality_note: CaO abundance derived from 1D CNN inversion of Clementine UVVIS 5-band reflectance (Qiu et al. 2025, Communications Earth & Environment). CNN-only product — not derivable from classical equation models due to complex spectral characteristics. LOOCV R²=0.918, second-highest of the five oxides. Global mean 14.93 wt%; bimodal distribution with modes at 10.63 wt% (maria) and 16.38 wt% (highlands/non-maria). Maria mean 11.28 wt%; non-maria mean 15.64 wt%. CaO co-varies with Al₂O₃ in the highlands (both enriched in plagioclase), and inversely in maria (clinopyroxene is Ca-rich but Al-poor). This map is therefore most informative when interpreted together with Al₂O₃ and FeO. The lunar south polar region CaO is consistent with non-mare composition. Key resource consideration: calcium-rich terrains (high CaO + high Al₂O₃) are dominated by anorthosite, relevant to both aluminum/calcium extraction and as a potential building material analog.
